source.title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let z(N0) be a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal. The paper proves that the range M(I-2S_-|z) of the operator I-2S_- acting on z(N0) can be closed with various finite or infinite codimensions. Determine whether the situation called case 3 can ever occur, namely whether there exists such an ideal z(N0) for which M(I-2S_-|z) is closed and has finite positive codimension 1, 2, 3, ... rather than codimension 0 or non-closed range.

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Find out whether case 3 is impossible.

accepted.question_text: Let z(N0) be a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal. Decide whether the situation called case 4 can ever occur, namely whether there exists such an ideal z(N0) for which the range M(I-2S_-|z) is closed and has infinite codimension.

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Find out whether case 4 is impossible.

accepted.question_text: For a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0), let S_- be the backward shift on z(N0) and let r(S_-|z) be its spectral radius. Determine whether the spectrum of S_- is always exactly the closed disk {lambda in C : |lambda| <= r(S_-|z)}.

For a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0), let S_+ and S_- denote the forward and backward shifts on z(N0), let r(S_+|z) and r(S_-|z) be their spectral radii, and let σ_Φ denote the Φ-spectrum. Determine whether the Φ-spectrum of each shift is always the closed annulus {lambda in C : r(S_\mp|z)^(-1) <= |lambda| <= r(S_\pm|z)}.

Let z(N0) be a shift-monotone sequence ideal, and let L^{APP}_z be the operator ideal consisting of all bounded operators S between Banach spaces for which the dyadic approximation-number sequence (a_{2^k}(S)) belongs to z(N0). Theorem 1.19 constructs traces on L^{APP}_z from (1/2)S_+-invariant linear forms φ on z(N0) by choosing a z-representation S=∑_{k>=0} S_k and setting φ_z(S)=φ((2^{-k} trace(S_k))_k). Show that every trace on L^{APP}_z is of this form, so that L^{APP}_z carries no traces other than those produced in Theorem 1.19.

evidence.quote:
Problem 5. Show that on LAPP
z there exist no other traces than those provided
by Theorem 1.19.

accepted.question_text: Let A be a quasi-Banach operator ideal of exact trace type 1/r, let d_{r,\infty}(N0) be the shift-monotone sequence ideal of sequences with dyadic decay O(2^{-k/r}), and let A^{APP}_{r,\infty} be the ideal of operators S in A for which the dyadic A-approximation numbers (a_{2^k}(S|A)) lie in d_{r,\infty}(N0). Theorem 1.21 constructs traces on A^{APP}_{r,\infty} from 2^{-1/r}S_+-invariant linear forms φ on d_{r,\infty}(N0) by choosing an (A,d_{r,\infty})-representation S=∑_{k>=0} S_k and setting φ_{r,\infty}(S|A)=φ((2^{-k/r} trace(S_k))_k). Show that every trace on A^{APP}_{r,\infty} is one of these traces.

evidence.quote:
Problem 6. Show that on AAPP
r,∞ there exist no other traces than those provided
by Theorem 1.21.

accepted.question_text: An operator ideal A is called traceless if it admits no nonzero trace. Show that every norm-closed operator ideal is traceless.

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Show that all norm–closed operator ideals are traceless.

accepted.question_text: Let z(N0) be a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal, and let L^{APP}_z be the corresponding operator ideal of Banach-space operators. For inessential operators, the paper defines a trace to be spectral when its value is determined by the eigenvalue sequence of the operator. Show that every trace on L^{APP}_z is spectral whenever z(N0) is quasi-Banach.

Problem 8. Show that all traces on LAPP

Determine whether this trace is spectral, meaning that for each operator in the ideal its value can be reconstructed from the operator's eigenvalue sequence.

accepted.question_text: For 1 <= r <= \infty, let L^{WEYL}_{r,\infty} be the quasi-Banach operator ideal defined by dyadic Weyl-number decay x_{2^k}(S)=O(2^{-k/r}), and let (L^{WEYL}_{r,\infty})^{APP}_{r,\infty} be the ideal obtained by applying the generalized approximation-number construction to L^{WEYL}_{r,\infty}. Determine whether the family (L^{WEYL}_{r,\infty})^{APP}_{r,\infty} strictly increases as r ranges over [2,\infty), or whether it becomes constant there; in particular, decide whether (L^{WEYL}_{2,\infty})^{APP}_{2,\infty}=L^{WEYL}_{1,\infty}.

Show that L^{APP}_z is contained in L^{ENT}_z for all shift-monotone sequence ideals z(N0).

accepted.context_brief: Concrete separation in the L^{APP}_{r,∞} scale.

accepted.question_text: Fix infinite-dimensional Banach spaces X and Y. Find large collections Z of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals such that (i) Z contains every Lorentz-type ideal d_{r,w}(N0), and (ii) the map z(N0) ↦ L^{APP}_z(X,Y) is one-to-one on Z.
accepted.context_brief: Injectivity of z ↦ L^{APP}_z(X,Y) on large classes.

Find large sets Z of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals that have

z (X, Y ) to Z is one-to-one.

accepted.question_text: Find infinite-dimensional Banach spaces X for which the set app(X) of approximation-number profiles realized by approximable operators on X is strictly smaller than the full cone c_0^*(N) of nonincreasing null sequences. In other words, find Banach spaces that have few approximable operators, and ideally make app(X) as small as possible.
accepted.context_brief: Banach spaces with few approximable operators.

Problem 21. Find infinite-dimensional Banach spaces that have few approx￾imable operators.

accepted.question_text: Find Banach spaces that contain an unconditional basic sequence but nevertheless have few approximable operators, meaning that their set app(X) of approximation-number profiles of approximable operators is strictly smaller than the full cone c_0^*(N).
accepted.context_brief: Few approximable operators despite unconditional structure.

accepted.question_text: Let X_K be the Argyros-Haydon C_0-trivial Banach space used in the paper's construction of the singular trace τ_Z on the quasi-Banach operator ideal N(2/3,Z). Describe the restriction of τ_Z to the component N(2/3,X_K)(\ell_2), and determine in particular whether this restriction might vanish identically on all of N(2/3,X_K)(\ell_2).

trace.notes: Resolved the user-supplied zbMATH record to the exact 2023 Springer paper and extracted the section map from the downloaded PDF. Open-problem content is concentrated in Section 2, pages 26-42.
Extracted 27 explicitly numbered open problems from Section 2.1 through Section 2.12 of the PDF. No implicit problems were needed because the source already provides an explicit numbered list.
No duplicates found. The paper's numbering 1-27 already partitions the open questions cleanly by topic.
Accepted all 27 items because each has an explicit problem label, a page citation, and enough surrounding source context to rewrite the statement self-containedly without adding unsupported facts.
